citation.title: Prolonged fasting identifies skeletal muscle mitochondrial dysfunction as consequence rather than cause of human insulin resistance

population.description: Twelve healthy, lean male volunteers with no family history of diabetes or other endocrine disorder (Table 1, mean ± SE). SDs computed as SE x sqrt(12): age 1.0 -> 3.46, BMI 0.5 -> 1.73. Crossover, all 12 in both conditions.

protocols.name: fast_12h
protocols.description: Single plasma sample after 12 h of fasting (calorie-free drinks only), Methods 'Experimental design' and Results 'Plasma parameters' (t = 12 h). Arm of 30 min read at minutes 29-30; the sample's clock hour is not printed: the fast follows a standardized evening meal and the 12 h sample is taken after the overnight fast, so the 12 h sample is put at 08:00, the 36 h sample at 08:00 + 24 h = 20:00 and the 60 h sample at 08:00 + 48 h = 08:00 (assumed); the paper's clinical day (leaving the chamber 'on the morning of the third day' at 60 h) agrees with the 60 h sample falling in the morning. H = 12 is the paper's t, counted from the start of the fast; the interval between the evening meal and the start of the fast is not printed.
